## About

Thirteen years in enterprise infrastructure. Five of them in product; the rest as the engineer
who built and ran the systems underneath it. A generalist AI PM whose differentiator is real
infrastructure depth — comfortable taking a product from a blank page to a working prototype.

## Work

### NetApp — Product Manager (2022 to now), Bangalore
Winning AI workloads for an enterprise platform. NetApp's object storage had to win the new wave
of AI and analytics workloads, not just the buyers it already had.
- Role: Product Manager. Owns the vision, roadmap, PRDs, and go-to-market for the product.
- What I did: Shipped features and third-party integrations that made the product compatible with
  AI applications. Wrote the PRDs that set workload priority and cut the team's planning cycle.
- Results: 65% YoY adoption growth · 25% faster planning cycle · 13 years in storage & infra.

## Builds (self-directed case studies)

One shipped MVP and three self-directed case studies, each taken from a blank page to something real.

### Build your own AI, not another search box · AI upskilling (shipped MVP)
Live product: https://kaamai.vercel.app
- Problem: Most non-technical professionals type one-off questions into ChatGPT and get generic
  answers back, nothing they keep. The people who get real leverage build their own AI, but "learn
  to build AI" usually means code, jargon, and a course they abandon.
- Role: Product manager and builder. Took it from problem and persona to a shipped, working product.
- What I built: A guided, gamified PWA that walks someone from a blank page to a real AI assistant
  they build in one sitting and keep. Plain HTML, CSS, and JS front end; a Supabase backend as the
  system of record for identity, the saved assistant, progress, and funnel analytics; offline-first
  sync; and email one-time-code login that works end to end.
- Shipped: Live and installable at kaamai.vercel.app as rung one of a reskilling ladder. The whole
  curriculum, every role and task, lives in JSON kept separate from the app, so content can grow
  without touching code.
- Metrics: 5-step build (blank page to live AI) · 36 role x task paths (9 roles x 4 tasks) · 45/45
  automated tests passing.

### Vendor onboarding, in one workflow — B2B SaaS
Prototype live: https://vendor-onboarding-mvp.vercel.app/admin
- Problem: Onboarding a vendor takes 15–30 business days across email, spreadsheets, and four
  separate systems, and nobody can see where a vendor is stuck.
- Role: Product manager and builder. Framed the problem, scoped the MVP, built the prototype.
- What I built: A self-service onboarding portal with role-based access and department SLAs, and a
  clearance model that runs Legal, Financial, Personnel, and Security checks in parallel — the whole
  vendor lifecycle modeled as a state machine.
- Outcome: Moves onboarding from a 15–30-day scramble to one tracked workflow every team can see.
- Metrics: 4 parallel clearances · 12 personas mapped · 15–30 days being cut.

### Saath — Someone shows up when it matters — Elder care
- Problem: India has 150 million elderly people, and formal senior care reaches barely 1% of them.
  Families living far away have no reliable way to know a parent is alright tonight.
- Role: Product manager and builder. Ran the research and shaped the product end to end.
- What I built: A monitoring service on contactless Wi-Fi sensing — no camera, no microphone,
  nothing to wear — paired with an app where every alert goes to a named person, not a group.
- Evidence: 49 interviews across families, doctors, nurses, and insurers; a Bengaluru pilot scoped
  with an NGO and a cardiac hospital.
- Metrics: 49 interviews run · 150M elderly in India · $8.9B silver economy.

### The last 200 metres nobody owns — Logistics
- Problem: India runs 7.8 million quick-commerce orders a day. The last stretch, from the society
  gate to the door, lands on security desks and riders; one 600-flat society pushes 280+ parcels a
  day through a single desk.
- Role: Product and business modeling. Built the operating model and the case for it.
- What I built: A micro-logistics hub at the gate — smart lockers, verified runners, and a
  15-minute delivery circuit — with unit economics and a seed-stage business case.
- Outcome: Unit economics move from 27% margin in month one to 48% by month twenty-four, with
  payback inside a few months.
- Metrics: ₹2,900 Cr total market · margin 27%→48% (month 1 to 24) · 7.8M orders a day.
